subject: Basic Science and Technology
examFormat: Basic Science and Technology (BST) combines Basic Science, Basic Technology, Physical and Health Education and Computer Studies. Basic Science: The BECE Basic Science and Technology syllabus aims to help candidates gain a fundamental understanding of science and technology, apply scientific and technological knowledge to address modern societal needs, and be equipped with essential knowledge for further studies in science and technology. Basic Science and Technology is examined in four compulsory papers (I–IV). The Basic Science component is examined in Paper I, which has 60 multiple-choice questions covering Basic Science together with Physical and Health Education, with an allocated time of sixty minutes. Basic Technology: The BECE Basic Science and Technology syllabus aims to help candidates gain a fundamental understanding of science and technology, apply scientific and technological knowledge to address modern societal needs, and be equipped with essential knowledge for further studies in science and technology. Basic Science and Technology is examined in four compulsory papers (I–IV). Basic Technology is examined in Paper II, which has 60 multiple-choice questions covering Basic Technology and Computer Studies with an allocated time of sixty minutes, and in Paper IV, which consists of three required Technical Drawing (practical) problems based on basic geometric constructions, to be done in 45 minutes. Physical and Health Education: The BECE Basic Science and Technology syllabus aims to help candidates gain a fundamental understanding of science and technology, apply scientific and technological knowledge to address modern societal needs, and be equipped with essential knowledge for further studies in science and technology. Basic Science and Technology is examined in four compulsory papers (I–IV). Physical and Health Education is examined in Paper I, which has 60 multiple-choice questions covering Basic Science together with Physical and Health Education, with an allocated time of sixty minutes. Computer Studies: The BECE Basic Science and Technology syllabus aims to help candidates gain a fundamental understanding of science and technology, apply scientific and technological knowledge to address modern societal needs, and be equipped with essential knowledge for further studies in science and technology. Basic Science and Technology is examined in four compulsory papers (I–IV). Computer Studies is examined in Paper II, which has 60 multiple-choice questions covering Basic Technology and Computer Studies with an allocated time of sixty minutes, and in Paper III, one Computer Studies practical question taken from an application package (such as CorelDraw, Paint, Instant Artist, Microsoft Word or a spreadsheet), to be finished in 45 minutes.
excluded: Built from the component subjects; see each component.
